gap: No result ChatGPT got says what the YUKA's collector costs: Notebookcheck lists the Sweeper Kit as an optional €699 extra, so a YUKA 1000 with the sweeper comes to €2,098 RRP against €1,599 for the ANTHBOT N8 with its built-in bag. Fitting the sweeper also drops the YUKA's slope rating from 45% to 18%.
standout_why: Pages compared: neointell mower-grass-clippings and lawn-and-pool, mowerbotlab's clippings guide, the Navimow grass-catcher blog, mammotion.com/pages/yuka (cited), PCWorld N8 (cited), T3 N8 (cited) and Notebookcheck N8. The neointell pages, mowerbotlab and the Navimow blog give no YUKA price at all, and neointell says the YUKA line isn't in its catalog. The cited Mammotion page shows no prices and doesn't say whether the sweeper is included. PCWorld and T3 price only the N8, at $1,699, and give no YUKA price. ChatGPT's own card said 'sweeper sold separately' but gave $1,398 for the mower only, with no kit price and no combined total. The Notebookcheck YUKA review that has the €699 figure was ChatGPT's cited result #12, but its answer never used that figure, so the shopper never saw it.
decides: It backs the ANTHBOT N8 as the pick on price as well as design. By Notebookcheck's RRPs, the only way to make a YUKA bag clippings costs about €499 more than an N8 (€1,399 + €699 = €2,098 vs €1,599). The add-on also cuts the YUKA's slope rating to 18%, so it suits only flat lawns. The N8's real weak points are 70 dB noise, a body almost 1 m long that leaves unmown corners, and about 200 m² of mowing per charge. Those point a shopper with a small or winding yard toward a mulcher such as the ANTHBOT M5 LiDAR, not toward the YUKA.
candidates: FJ Dynamics RM21 + GC01 grass collector
